messages:
sanjay: FYI observed a p99 tail bump on the 2x-gpu pool after yesterday's kernel-selector changes. p95 steady but p99 up ~110ms. tagging eng-runtime for triage.

emmabar: can you drop the trace snippets? trying to see if this is KV miss related or a kernel handoff problem.

sanjay: pasted a sample from the perf trace: 
```
profile dump @ 2026-03-17T22:47
req: xyz-987
seq_len: 48
chosen_kernel: generic_int8_fallback
kv_hit: false
queue_ms: 12
exec_ms: 46
kv_populate_ms: 22
total_ms: 92
```

emmabar: kv_populate 22ms on misses explains a chunk of the tail. also queue_ms 12ms contributes. what's the route scheduler config?

kevin: route uses max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=30. Our adaptive heuristics sometimes create uneven microbatches (tiny requests + medium ones) causing selector to choose the compatibility kernel.

nicole: i've seen that pattern: when batch token distribution is skewed the selector falls back to generic kernels. fused kernels give lower p99 but can hurt throughput if the batch shapes are suboptimal.

sanjay: thinking we have three levers: 1) tighten max_wait_ms for short seqs, 2) add lightweight KV priming for routes with rising miss rates, 3) tweak kernel-scoring to prefer fast kernels when tradeoff ok.

kevin: proposed A/B config to test (per-route):
```
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 3072
  adaptive_waits:
    threshold_tokens: 256
    short_max_wait_ms: 8
    default_max_wait_ms: 24
  burst_backoff: true
  burst_backoff_window_ms: 60
```

emmabar: recommend also a KV priming rule: if kv_miss_rate > 4% over 5m, trigger async prime for top-5 hot keys for that route. small CPU cost but reduces on-path kv_populate.

nicole: i ran the simulator over recent request corpus with those params. outcome: p95 ~unchanged, p99 improved ~70-85ms depending on traffic shape. throughput loss ~2-4% at peak in synthetic runs. kernel fallback rate dropped ~10%.

runtime-oncall: for rollout guardrails: canary to 5% qps, monitor p95/p99, kv_miss_rate, error_rate. rollback if p99 regresses >10% or error_rate >0.1% sustained 10m. I'll create the canary job.

devops-bot: Canary created -> 2026-03-18T01:30Z. Rollback triggers: p99 +10% OR errors >0.1% for 10m. Notifying @runtime-oncall.

kevin: note we should expose per-route override flags and a low-latency tier so we don't apply this cluster-wide. enterprise routes that value throughput can opt out.

emmabar: i'll add an evaluation script that scores routes by sequence length histogram and latency sensitivity; it'll recommend whether to opt-in for the low-latency scheduling.

sanjay: action items: 
- emmabar: PR for KV priming + route candidate metric (small change).
- nicole: run a 12h canary sim and post batch token distribution histograms.
- runtime-oncall: run canary and watch roll metrics.
- kevin: implement per-route config toggles and default to conservative values.

kevin: will push toggles and sane defaults.
nicole: will post canary sim summary here soon with graphs. :thumbsup:

sanjay: thanks all. want to keep customer-facing tails under 250ms; please escalate if rollout shows regression.
